question: Should OpenClaw adopt operator-selected core readiness criteria and `registerReadinessCriterion` as supported core and plugin contracts after the framework PR lands?
rationale: The patch adds durable config semantics and a new plugin API whose permanent ownership, upgrade promise, and fail-closed behavior require maintainer intent rather than a mechanical repair decision.

options.title: Approve the stacked contract
options.body: Keep this PR as the owner-adoption layer after the framework lands, with explicit API and upgrade review plus live behavior proof.

options.title: Narrow to internal observations
options.body: Retain only core-owned observations and defer plugin registration or operator promotion until a narrower plugin SDK contract is approved.

options.title: Pause the adoption layer
options.body: Keep the framework independent and defer these criteria until hosting-profile or deployment requirements establish the needed core scope.

recommendation.title: Approve the stacked contract
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as the owner-adoption layer after the framework lands, with explicit API and upgrade review plus live behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They hold the strongest available technical context across the linked readiness framework and the proposed owner-adoption layer; a repository core owner must make the final product decision.
